note: A Friesian's markings, and a fixed colour rather than a tint on purpose.

They used to ask for the second colour of the palette, and a cow's palettes are one colour apiece — the tint index is clamped to what the palette has, so the patch was handed the hide colour and vanished into it. Black and white is the whole point, so it is stated here and holds on the brown and tan cows too.
One patch per flank, off-centre and at different sizes, so the two sides do not mirror.
